tasks.title: The Stolen Necklace
tasks.summary: During her daughter's wedding feast, Kamala's pearl necklace vanished from a locked room. She begs the court to name the thief.
clues: The room's only window is barred. The thief came through the door.
There is one key. Kamala wears it on her waist-cord — except while she bathed, when it hung on a peg by the courtyard well.
Raghu the servant boy drew water at that well all evening. He swears he never left it.
Cousin Madhav arrived late with fresh henna on his palms. The lid of the jewel box bears an orange smudge.
Sundari, the neighbour's daughter, sang with the women through the whole feast; twenty guests heard her.

options.label: Raghu, the servant boy
options.outcome: The boy is flogged, the necklace never found. Weeks later Madhav is seen selling pearls in the next town.

options.label: Madhav, the late-arriving cousin
options.outcome: Confronted with the henna-stained lid, Madhav breaks down; the pearls are found sewn into his sash. He pays a fine to the crown.

options.label: Sundari, the neighbour's daughter
options.outcome: Twenty wedding guests protest her innocence. The court's judgement becomes a bazaar joke.

options.label: Fine the whole household
options.outcome: The crown's coffers gain a little, but the widow is shamed and the thief walks free.

tasks.title: The Cheating Scales
tasks.petitioner: The market inspector of the grain bazaar
tasks.summary: A grain merchant is accused of cheating with a false weight. Exactly one of his four weights — marked 1, 2, 3 and 5 seers — is false. The inspector tested them on the royal balance.
clues: The 1-seer weight balanced the crown's own 1-seer standard.
The 1-seer and 2-seer together balanced the 3-seer.
The 3-seer and 2-seer together were set against the 5-seer: the 5-seer's pan rose.
Only one weight is false.

options.label: The 1-seer weight
options.outcome: The 1-seer matched the crown standard — the court is laughed at, and the crown pays the merchant for his trouble.

options.label: The 2-seer weight
options.outcome: If the 2-seer were false, 1 + 2 could not have balanced 3. The merchant is compensated; the real cheat continues.

options.label: The 3-seer weight
options.outcome: The 3-seer agreed with 1 + 2. The accusation collapses and the crown pays damages.

options.label: The 5-seer weight is light
options.outcome: The 5-seer is shaved underneath. The merchant is fined and every shop in the bazaar rushes to have its weights stamped.

tasks.title: Birbal's Line
tasks.prompt: The emperor draws a line on the floor of the court: "Make this line shorter — but you may not touch, erase or cut it." How?

options.label: Pour sand over half of it
Draw a longer line beside it
Fold the carpet it is drawn on
Proclaim that it is shorter

tasks.explanation: Birbal drew a longer line beside the emperor's. Without being touched, the first line had become the shorter one.

tasks.title: The Court Trial: The Missing Tribute
tasks.summary: Five hundred gold coins of tribute vanished from the sealed treasury vault during the night. Each of you holds a different record. Share what you know, weigh it, and let the Raja pronounce the verdict before the lamps burn out.

suspects.name: Bhima, the vault guard
suspects.description: On duty all night at the vault door.

suspects.name: Vishnudatta, the royal scribe
suspects.description: Keeps the tribute ledger and carries the vault seal.

suspects.name: Dhanpal, the merchant
suspects.description: Delivered the tribute chests yesterday; known gambler.

suspects.name: Lalita, the palace cook
suspects.description: Brings the night guard his meal at the third watch.

tasks.explanation: The vault was opened with a true impression of the scribe's seal — and the seal never leaves him. He rewrote the ledger in fresh ink, and paid off his debts and bought a horse with new gold the very next morning. Dhanpal was at the dice house; Bhima logged the opening honestly.

clues.text: Third watch: vault opened with the scribe's seal, then resealed. Guard on duty: Bhima. No forced entry.
The tribute page was rewritten — the ink is still fresh. The hand is the scribe's, or a very good copy of it.
Merchant Dhanpal spent the night at the dice house; a dozen gamblers saw him lose. At dawn the scribe bought a horse, paying in new gold coins.
The cook Lalita says Bhima was awake when she brought his meal, grumbling that the scribe 'never lets that seal out of his sight'.
By custom the vault seal never leaves the scribe's person. A copied seal leaves a crooked edge — last night's wax shows a clean, true impression.
The scribe's family lands failed two harvests running. Moneylenders in his village say he owed them heavily — until yesterday.
You recall signing no order to open the vault last night.

success.outcome: The scribe's saddlebags hold the missing gold. The court has seen that the powerful are not above the law.

failure.outcome: An innocent is punished while the true thief rides away with the tribute. Whispers of injustice fill the bazaar.

tasks.title: Sunset Edict — Day of Justice
tasks.summary: The lamps are lit. The Raja must issue one edict before the court rises.

edicts.label: Proclaim a festival of lamps
edicts.description: Spend from the treasury to lift the people's spirits.

edicts.label: Raise the salt tax
edicts.description: Fill the treasury at the cost of goodwill.

edicts.label: Survey and measure the fields
edicts.description: Assess the land fairly so revenue follows the true harvest.

tasks.title: The Dry Well Dispute
tasks.summary: In the drought, only one stepwell still holds water. Palashpur's ancestors dug it; Kanakgram's fields lie closer. Both villages have come armed with sticks.
clues: Palashpur has a second, shallower well that is nearly dry.
Kanakgram grows the grain that feeds the capital's market.
The crown's masons are idle until the rains.

options.label: Award the well to Palashpur, who dug it
options.outcome: Custom is honoured, but Kanakgram's fields wither and grain prices climb in the capital.

options.label: Share it by turns, with a crown officer keeping the rota
options.outcome: Water flows to both villages on alternate days. The sticks are put away.

options.label: Build Kanakgram a new stepwell at crown expense
options.outcome: Costly — but the idle masons cut a fine stepwell that will outlast everyone in this court.

tasks.title: Whose Mango Tree?
tasks.summary: Two neighbours each claim the mango tree in the lane between their houses. Neither has a deed; each brings a witness. How does the court find the true owner?
clues: Each man's witness turns out to be his own cousin.
The owner has watered and guarded the tree for twelve years.
The other man only wants the fruit.

options.label: Split the fruit equally each season
options.outcome: Peace for a season — but the man who tended the tree for twelve years feels robbed.

options.label: Send word at night that thieves are stripping the tree, and watch who runs to guard it
options.outcome: Ramu sprints out with a lamp and a stick; Shamu rolls over and sleeps. The tree is Ramu's — and the lane laughs at Shamu for a month.

options.label: Cut the tree down and divide the wood
options.outcome: A twelve-year tree is lost to settle a quarrel. The court is called foolish.

options.label: Award it to the elder of the two
options.outcome: Age is not ownership. The real owner appeals, and the dispute drags on.

tasks.title: Sugar from Sand
tasks.prompt: A jar of sugar has been mixed with sand. Separate them — without water, fire or any tool, and without lifting a finger yourself.

options.label: Winnow it in the wind
Wait for the rains to wash it
Scatter it beside an anthill
Let the camels graze on it

tasks.explanation: Birbal scattered the mixture near an anthill. By morning, the ants had carried off every grain of sugar and left the sand behind.

tasks.title: The Famine
tasks.summary: The monsoon failed in the eastern villages. Relief carts leave at dusk. Pledge grain and gold from your own purse — in secret. The Treasurer may also open the royal granary. Only the Sitadhyaksha knows how much the villages truly need.
tasks.rumouredNeed: Reports differ wildly — ask the Sitadhyaksha.

success.outcome: The carts reach every village. Not one child starves, and the eastern farmers will remember this court.

failure.outcome: The carts arrive half-empty. Families flee west, and the fields go unsown next season.

tasks.title: Sunset Edict — Day of Hunger
tasks.summary: The relief carts are gone. What will the Raja decree so this never happens again?

edicts.label: Open the royal granaries to the poor
edicts.description: Immediate relief from the crown's stores.

edicts.label: Build a stone weir to feed a canal
edicts.description: A great work of masonry to tame the river, as the Cholas did.

edicts.label: Post guards against grain hoarders
edicts.description: Punish those who profit from hunger.

tasks.title: The Stranger at the Gate
tasks.petitioner: The captain of the western gate
tasks.summary: A horse trader from beyond the western passes asks to enter the city. His saddlebags hold fine horses' papers — and hand-drawn maps of our roads.
clues: Scouts report dust clouds beyond the western hills.
Foreign traders have enriched the city for generations.
The maps mark every well on the road to our walls.

options.label: Arrest him and seize the maps
options.outcome: The maps are burned, but whoever sent him simply sends another — and now knows we are watching.

options.label: Welcome him — and have him shadowed by a spy disguised as a wandering ascetic
options.outcome: He leads our 'ascetic' straight to an enemy camp. We learn their numbers and approach.

options.label: Welcome him openly and buy his horses
options.outcome: Good horses — but the 'trader' slips away at night with our road maps complete.

tasks.title: The Temple Elephants
tasks.summary: An enemy army approaches and the fort needs war elephants. The town temple keeps twelve for its festivals.
clues: The temple festival falls next month.
Elephants can batter down a gate — or break one.
The treasury is watched closely by the people.

options.label: Requisition the temple elephants
options.outcome: The army gains its elephants; the priests curse the court from the temple steps.

options.label: Rent them at a fair price for the season
options.outcome: The temple is paid and honoured; the elephants march with garlands on their tusks.

options.label: Leave the elephants; train workers as foot soldiers
options.outcome: Farmers become soldiers. The fields feel their absence, but the temple is untouched.

tasks.title: Fill the Hall
tasks.prompt: "Fill this great hall from floor to ceiling, every corner of it — and spend no more than a single copper coin." What do you buy?

options.label: A cartload of straw
One oil lamp
A sack of sand
A crow, to fill it with noise

tasks.explanation: One small lamp, lit at dusk, filled the whole hall with light — every corner, for a single copper coin.

tasks.title: Defend the Fort
tasks.summary: Three waves will strike the four gates. Only the Spy Chief sees where the enemy masses. Only the Senapati can move troops — and cannot see the enemy. The Mahamantri may parley once per wave to weaken the largest force, and the Treasurer may buy reinforcements.

success.outcome: The enemy breaks against the walls and retreats. Bards will sing of this siege.

failure.outcome: The gates are breached and the lower town is sacked before the enemy is driven back.

tasks.title: Sunset Edict — Day of the Siege
tasks.summary: The last lamps of the cycle. Issue your final edict — and, if you dare, name the traitor in your court.

edicts.label: Plant shade trees and dig wells along the roads
edicts.description: Comfort for every traveller, man and beast.

edicts.label: Build sarais and a horse-post along the trunk road
edicts.description: Rest-houses and swift messengers bind the realm together.

edicts.label: Rebuild and strengthen the walls
edicts.description: Never again shall the gates tremble.
